title: Toss Ball
summary: The hovering aerial manipulator starts with a small red ball held between its gripper fingers, and an open-top grey storage bin stands on the ground some distance ahead of it. Deliver the ball into the bin: at some control step the ball must be inside the bin's volume and clear of the gripper while the robot's airframe is at least 0.7 m short of the bin's centre along the robot's initial forward direction.
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane; there is no wall or other fixture. Ahead of the robot an immovable (kinematic) grey plastic storage container, an open-top tote 40 x 30 x 17 cm, rests on the ground; its forward distance and sideways offset vary between instances. A red ball, 8 cm in diameter, is a free rigid body: at every reset it is placed at the gripper's tool tip between the fingers and the gripper is commanded closed, so the robot starts holding it; once let go it falls under gravity. Nothing else moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the bin, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Container: container.usd, whose geometry is a payload (NVIDIA warehouse asset Container_B06_40x30x17cm, 'Gray' variant, convex-decomposition collision) referenced from NVIDIA's Omniverse content server; kinematic rigid body, scale (1, 1, 1) (container_size (0.4, 0.3, 0.17) m divided by the nominal size (0.4, 0.3, 0.17) m). At each reset (mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) its root is placed at (2.3 + cx', 0.0 + cy', 0.0) m with cx', cy' ~ U(-0.5, 0.5) m independently, orientation identity, zero velocity. Ball: sphere radius 0.04 m, mass 0.01 kg, colour (0.95, 0.05, 0.05), default rigid-body properties (gravity on), scene default physics material (friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0). At each reset, after the robot has been reset, the ball is placed at the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + R(ee_link) (0.18, 0, 0)) with the ee_link orientation and zero velocity, and the gripper target is set to closed (-1, the finger joints' lower limit, 0.001 m per the URDF); the FA-Hexa defines no object-width converter, so the finger joints are not preset to the ball's width.
success: Success at a control step when all three hold at once: (1) ball_released: the distance from the ball centre to the gripper tool-tip point (ee_link position + R(ee_link) (0.18, 0, 0)) is >= 0.12 m; (2) the ball centre is inside (bounds inclusive) the world-axis-aligned box x in [cx - 0.20, cx + 0.20], y in [cy - 0.15, cy + 0.15], z in [cz, cz + 0.17], where (cx, cy, cz) is the container's root position (cz = 0), i.e. the full nominal 0.40 (x) x 0.30 (y) x 0.17 (z) m container size above its root; (3) robot_behind_bin: base_link x <= cx - 0.7. The ball need not come to rest: being inside the box at one step is enough. AM-Bench reports ball_released and ball_delivered as subtask criteria. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 10 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 1200 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 1199th step.
difficulty_note: The airframe must stay at least 0.7 m short of the bin centre (along x) at the moment the ball is in the bin, the bin's position changes per instance, and the episode lasts only 10 s.
standard_notes: Neither the bin's position nor the ball's state is given: the bin has to be found with the forward-looking onboard cameras (the held ball sits just in front of the end-effector camera), and whether the ball got in can only be judged visually. The airframe's distance to the bin must be estimated from the images together with the base pose from proprioception.
